claim: Traffic signals adapt through emergent pattern formation where each intersection follows simple rules based on local conditions, creating system-level optimization
mechanism: Each intersection follows a simple rule set (e.g., increase green time if queue length exceeds threshold, decrease if queue is zero) that, when applied across the network, creates emergent patterns that optimize flow
evidence: Emergent behavior appears in other complex systems
Some traffic signal systems use simple heuristic rules
assumptions: Simple local rules can produce complex global optimization
The network will self-organize into optimal patterns
No explicit communication between intersections is needed
expected_failure_modes: Failure to adapt to non-recurrent congestion patterns
novelty_rationale: Directly transfers the myxomycete emergent computation principle to traffic signal control through simple local rules
testability: Can be tested by implementing simple rule-based signal control and measuring system performance
falsifier: If the simple rules fail to produce optimal flow patterns or create oscillations or instabilities in the network
